title: David Humphreys to Pickering, Madrid, 1799: the coded parts of despatches Nos. 188 and 214, read with his code rebuilt from the State Department's decipherments

documents.shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Despatches from U.S. Ministers to Spain, vol. 4, microfilm M31 roll 5 (catalog record 188602965), frames 0414-0417; Humphreys's No. 214

plaintext.source: No decipherment on or after this copy (frames 0410-0429; 0418-0429 are enclosures); no second copy on M31 rolls 5-7. Not found in Naval Documents, Quasi-War (vol. 4, text search), American State Papers, Foreign Relations vol. 2, the Pickering Papers calendar or F. L. Humphreys 1917.

documents.shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Despatches from U.S. Ministers to Spain, vol. 4, microfilm M31 roll 5 (catalog record 188602965), frame 0364, left page; despatch of April 1799, number not read

plaintext.source: Bare on this copy; print not searched.

transcription.source: National Archives Catalog image, one crop
transcription.notes: Transcribed once after the freeze and checked twice on the same crop; the first session's inventory estimated 19 groups at overview size, the transcription has 16.

system.summary: One-part scrambled numerical code of about 1,600 elements (numbers 2-1590 seen) for words, syllables, single letters and punctuation, with a few homophones: Jefferson's 'Code No. 8' of 1785 (Boyd), Weber's unlocated '994 = the' code.

diacritics.note: Numbers only; capitals and accents not coded.

prior_solution.where: For Nos. 188 and 214 none found: no decipherment on or after either copy on the film, no second copy on M31 rolls 5-7, and no print (Naval Documents, Quasi-War vols. 2 and 4; American State Papers, Foreign Relations vol. 2; Pickering Papers calendar; F. L. Humphreys 1917). Whether the Department deciphered the copies it received first is not established. The code itself: the State Department's clerks deciphered other despatches in it (our crib); the Papers of Thomas Jefferson decoded the 1791 letters with a partially reconstructed Code No. 8 (communication from James P. McClure, 2012, unpublished); F. L. Humphreys (1917) printed the 1791 letters decoded by 'Dr. Lowndes'; the Madison Papers print Jacob Wagner's decodings of March 1801.

conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling set the task and the rules (freeze the table before a held-out test written down first, two transcriptions, every context value marked) and ran the agents; AI agents paged the film, transcribed, built and tested the table, read the passages, searched the prior work and checked the result. No person has checked a reading on the image.
tools: macOS Vision OCR and the catalog text layer to find code pages on the film
Python: pairs, table build, held-out test with shuffled tables, reading marks (scripts/)
image crops of the catalog images

solution.what: Downloaded every frame of M31 rolls 4, 5 and 6, M43 rolls 2 and 3 and M31 roll 7 frames 0003-0214 from the National Archives Catalog (one request at a time), and searched them with our OCR and the catalog text layer for code pages; inventory of 16 despatches in this code (inventory.tsv).

Identified the code as Boyd's Code No. 8 (994 = the) from the Papers of Thomas Jefferson, the Papers of John Adams, Weber and Cryptiana; found that the Jefferson Papers editors hold an unpublished partial reconstruction; no target or lead upstream.

Transcribed the crib pages (1791 Nos. 10 and 11; 1800-01 interlined despatches; the 30 March 1801 postscript) and aligned them group by group to the clerks' decipherments and to the printed decoded texts: 3,368 pairs; built a table of 686 groups (key/table_frozen_v1.tsv).

Froze the table (sha256 2c2358a4...a98cd1) after writing the test plan; held-out No. 262 (24 Feb 1801): 129 of 135 scored groups decode to the clerk's element (95.6%), precision 99.2%; 200 shuffled tables at most 3.0%. Stricter count by a second agent, whole words carried by one group: 74 of 78, shuffled at most 3.

Compared the table with the codes of Weber's appendix (WE016-WE028), Code No. 16, King's 769 code, Carmichael's 1196 code, Code No. 10 and Pinckney's 1651 code at the same numbers and at offsets: none is a relative.
Transcribed the coded parts of Nos. 188 (56 groups) and 214 (352 groups) twice, the second pass from the end backwards; identical. 12 groups of No. 214 have digits hidden in the binding.
Decoded Nos. 214, 188 and the April 1799 sentence with the frozen table; groups the table lacks or gives wrongly were given context values, kept in a separate file and marked by basis (H, P, S).

Independent check by a second AI agent: 40 of 40 sampled pairs confirmed on the image; own transcription of No. 188 and of No. 214 passages a and e (one misread corrected) and group-by-group check of f-j; test rerun; content wording corrected (Basle, Saavedra, voted, trade, Sweden, de Staël marked as context or inference).

Second pass of the crib pages M43-02-0046, 0047, 0052, 0053 and M31-006-0253, 0254 from the end backward: 1,533 of 1,541 groups agree; corrections recorded after the test (key/corrections_after_test.tsv); the frozen table unchanged.

Searched for other copies of Nos. 188 and 214 (none on rolls 5-7) and for prior print (Naval Documents, American State Papers, Pickering Papers calendar, F. L. Humphreys 1917): none. History read in Turner 1905; Whitaker, Lyon and DeConde not reached; Humphreys's papers at Yale not checked.

After the test, while packaging: No. 73 (29 May 1793, M43-02-0285), not in the build, decodes to the clerk's separate decipherment for 16 of 17 groups (the 17th has no table value). Not pre-registered.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 364 tokens, 179 types, en-modern order 4: reading -1.842 per letter; random keys -2.665 (z 9.6); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -1.823 (mean -1.85, z 0.4); annealer on the real text -1.793. Verdict: underdetermined.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -1.842; polyphony 0.003; 60 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -1.793

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext

credits.note: Andrew Beling, with AI agents: table of the code rebuilt from the clerks' decipherments with every pair cited to roll, frame and line, held-out test, transcriptions and readings of the coded parts of Nos. 188 and 214 and of the April 1799 sentence.

The State Department's clerks (Jacob Wagner in 1801, per the Madison Papers): decipherments between the lines of Humphreys's despatches and on a separate sheet (No. 73): the source of 1,199 of the 3,460 pairs (the rest are aligned to printed decoded texts) and the reference of the held-out test.

Papers of Thomas Jefferson 18:472-75, 497-98: the decoded texts of Nos. 10 and 11 (1791), to which the 1791 pairs without a legible gloss are aligned; the editors decoded or verified them with their partially reconstructed Code No. 8 (unpublished).

A partial reconstruction of Code No. 8 exists in the editors' files ('Code No. 8 partial key, communication from James P. McClure, 20 April 2012', cited in the Papers of John Adams 17); not seen by us.
Papers of James Madison, Secretary of State Series 1:50-53: Wagner's decoding of the postscript of 30 March 1801, to which the pairs of M31-006-0284 are aligned.

Life and Times of David Humphreys: the 1791 letters decoded by 'Dr. Lowndes', and the coded part of No. 262 (24 Feb 1801) in italics, used with the clerk's interlining as the reference of the held-out test.

texts.label: Coded parts of No. 214, 6 August 1799 (ten passages)
texts.summary: Humphreys can account for Spain's wavering over the Spanish minister Yrujo's recall only by supposing that Yrujo shares, with certain lea[d?][ing?] [men?] at Madrid, in the profits of an exclusive [trade?] from the United States to the Spanish colonies; asks whether to stay at Lisbon or go home if forced to leave Spain; tells Urquijo of his own belief that France had {never} given up its design on Louisiana ("re[197][1355]ished", read as "relinquished", is mostly guessed), and reports Urquijo's assurance that France {should} {never} get it while he remained in office.

texts.label: Coded passage of No. 188, 19 March 1799
texts.summary: The Swedish chargé at Madrid (from the enclosures) gave Humphreys reason to believe (the reading, word for word) "that the government of [Sweden?] {now} less [inclin?]d to use management with that of France ... and that it is even probable the Baron [935] sta[ël?] would soon retire from Paris"; fills the asterisks in Naval Documents, Quasi-War 2:437.

outcome.notes: Status: in progress, folder only. The code is known to scholarship (Boyd's Code No. 8); its key is lost and the Jefferson Papers' partial reconstruction is unpublished. The readings of Nos. 188 and 214 were not found in print or on the film.
